newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended ahead on Thursday, getting a late boost from a short squeeze in Bund futures after range trading through the afternoon, dealers said.
Cash business continued to be subdued though with institutional buyers still sidelined, one said, and the market would remain short of data to focus on until the end of the month.

Spreads to Germany at the longer end were again under pressure, with the ten-year yield discount narrowing to 11 basis points from 14 at the start of the week. In shorter maturities, however, Guilders found some outperformance.

The Dutch market started lower, feeling the drag from Treasuries, before recovering to spend most of the day narrowly ahead. A shakeout of shorts in the September Bund future contract provided the impetus into the close.
Despite the poor start and a gloomy mood in the U.S., the Dutch market seemed underpinned by positive sentiment and keen for opportunities to move higher, one broker said.
